title: Target engagement and efficacy in disease-modifying trials of synuclein-related disorders
title_zh: 突触蛋白相关疾病疾病修饰试验中的靶点结合与疗效
abstract: Abstract Disease-modifying trials in Parkinson’s disease (PD), multiple system atrophy (MSA) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) increasingly incorporate fluid and imaging biomarkers to demonstrate target engagement, de-risk subsequent phases of drug development and provide mechanistic evidence of biological activity. Whether biomarker modulation predicts clinical benefit remains unclear. We conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant review of phase II and III disease-modifying trials (2020–2025) that included at least one biomarker intended to assess target engagement. Twenty-six trials met inclusion criteria (PD = 19, MSA = 4, DLB = 3; n = 2195 participants). Target engagement was reported in 14 of 19 PD trials (12 phase II/2 phase III), 1 of 4 MSA trials and 2 of 3 DLB trials (all phase II). Concordance between target engagement and clinical improvement was uncommon, as only 8/26 studies (7 phase II/1 phase III) demonstrated both target engagement and statistically significant clinical benefit, and just two of these (both phase II, one in PD and one in MSA) were rigorously controlled with low or moderate risk of bias. Nine trials showed target engagement without clinical benefit, whereas two reported clinical improvement without measurable target engagement. Baseline biomarker-guided patient selection was uncommon and rarely aligned with the compound’s mechanism of action. Patient-reported outcomes were widely used but rarely improved. Across recent disease-modifying trials in PD, DLB and MSA, target engagement was frequently demonstrated, yet clinical benefit rarely followed. These findings question the predictive value of currently used target-engagement biomarkers and highlight the need to biologically align trial populations with the mechanisms targeted by experimental molecular interventions.
abstract_zh: 摘要 在帕金森病（PD）、多系统萎缩（MSA）和路易体痴呆（DLB）的疾病修饰性试验中，越来越多地采用液体和影像生物标志物来证明靶点结合、降低药物研发后续阶段的风险，并提供生物学活性的机制证据。生物标志物调节是否预测临床获益仍不明确。我们进行了一项符合PRISMA（系统评价和Meta分析报告优选项目）标准的系统评价，回顾了2020年至2025年期间包含至少一项旨在评估靶点结合的生物标志物的II期和III期疾病修饰性试验。共26项试验符合纳入标准（PD 19项，MSA 4项，DLB 3项；n = 2195名参与者）。19项PD试验中有14项报告了靶点结合（12项II期/2项III期），4项MSA试验中有1项，3项DLB试验中有2项（均为II期）。靶点结合与临床改善的一致性较少见，仅8/26项研究（7项II期/1项III期）同时显示出靶点结合和统计学上显著的临床获益，而其中仅两项（均为II期，一项在PD，一项在MSA）采用了严格的对照设计，偏倚风险为低或中等。九项试验显示出靶点结合但无临床获益，而两项试验报告了可测的靶点结合而无临床改善。基于基线生物标志物的患者选择不常见，且很少与化合物的作用机制相一致。患者报告结局被广泛使用，但很少得到改善。在PD、DLB和MSA的近期疾病修饰性试验中，靶点结合经常得到证明，但临床获益却很少随之而来。这些发现对目前使用的靶点结合生物标志物的预测价值提出了质疑，并强调需要将试验人群与实验性分子干预所针对的机制在生物学上保持一致。
